card.summary: The Child Care Modernization Act of 2025 updates and reauthorizes the Child Care and Development Block Grant Act of 1990. The bill establishes new authorization levels for appropriations through fiscal year 2030, sets requirements for state plans regarding child care payment rates and cost estimation models, expands definitions for eligible activities and children, and creates a new grant program focused on child care supply and facilities.

summary: The Child Care Modernization Act of 2026 amends and reauthorizes the Child Care and Development Block Grant Act of 1990 through fiscal year 2031. It updates definitions for eligible children and activities, requires states to use a cost-estimation model for provider payment rates over time, establishes new supply and facilities grants for child care providers, and mandates additional state reporting and reviews of health and safety requirements.

affected_groups.effect: Gain expanded definitions of eligible activities allowing access to child care, standardized sliding fee copayment scales, and potential improvements in child care availability and affordability.
Eligible providers are impacted by updated state payment rates based on cost-estimation models, new grant opportunities for facility upgrades and startup costs, and professional development support.
Must develop cost-estimation models, consult with stakeholders on state plans, conduct health and safety requirement reviews, submit progress and financial reports, and manage new grant distribution.

key_provisions: Authorizes appropriations such as may be necessary for fiscal years 2027 through 2031 for child care services, and fiscal years 2028 through 2031 for child care supply and facilities grants.
Expands definitions of eligible activities for parents (such as job training, education, health treatment, and leave under the Family and Medical Leave Act) and child eligibility criteria.

Requires state plans to adopt a statistically valid and reliable cost-estimation model for direct payment rates for child care providers within a set timeframe to cover operational costs and staff salaries.
Creates a new grant program for child care supply and facilities to provide startup, expansion, and facilities subgrants to qualified providers, prioritizing underserved populations.
Directs states to review health and safety requirements to eliminate redundancies, and requires states to submit annual reports on family spending and progress toward benchmarks.
Requires the Secretary of Agriculture to revise federal regulations to exclude licensed or registered child care providers from certain Department of Agriculture loan restrictions.
missing_information: The exact dollar amounts authorized to be appropriated are not specified in the text, as the bill uses 'such sums as may be necessary'.
summary_detail.plain_summary: The Child Care Modernization Act of 2026 amends and reauthorizes the Child Care and Development Block Grant Act of 1990 through fiscal year 2031. It updates definitions for eligible children and activities, requires states to use a cost-estimation model for provider payment rates over time, establishes new supply and facilities grants for child care providers, and mandates additional state reporting and reviews of health and safety requirements.
summary_detail.significance: The bill updates and funds federal block grant programs and facilities grants supporting child care systems across states and territories. It affects state administrative duties, provider payment structures, and child care access parameters for families over a multi-year authorization period spanning fiscal years 2027 through 2031.
